[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Container Security and Kubernetes Hardening Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Securing containerized workloads and Kubernetes clusters requires a defense-in-depth approach. This tutorial covers best practices for image scanning, runtime security, and cluster hardening."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Container Image Security"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Minimizing the attack surface begins with the base image. Always use minimal base images like Alpine or distroless containers to reduce vulnerabilities."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scan images for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) during the CI/CD pipeline."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid running containers as the root user. Define a specific non-root user in your Dockerfile."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"FROM alpine:3.18
RUN addgroup -S appgroup && adduser -S appuser -G appgroup
USER appuser
CMD ["echo", "Secure container running"]"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Kubernetes Pod Hardening"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Kubernetes allows you to enforce security constraints on pods using SecurityContext. Never run privileged containers unless strictly necessary."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secured-pod
spec:
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 10001
    fsGroup: 10001
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: my-secure-app:latest
    securityContext:
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      capabilities:
        drop:
        - ALL"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Network Policies"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, Kubernetes pods are non-isolated and accept traffic from any source. Implement Network Policies to restrict pod-to-pod communication based on the principle of least privilege."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-ingress
  namespace: production
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"By implementing secure base images, enforcing strict Pod Security Standards, and utilizing Network Policies, you significantly reduce the risk of lateral movement and cluster compromise."}]
